rationale: The full randomized tulsi–cardamom trial reports lower older-adult depression score ranks than green tea at eight weeks. The comparison varies both plants and cannot identify a cardamom component effect. The Crohn trial uses cardamom in both arms, and the perinatal feeding work does not measure depression. Oral cardamom oil improves forced-swim behavior and increases locomotion in a reserpine model. The full behavioral values remain unverified and altered locomotion can affect immobility. The frozen culinary exposure and Parkinson endpoint remain open.

One randomized non-Parkinson depression trial reports lower DASS-21 scores when nigella oil extract is added to sertraline versus sertraline alone (PMID35548175, 18.6 vs 23.4, p<.001, with a one-point arithmetic discrepancy in printed change). A ground-seed premenstrual trial favored a composite mood domain rather than depression severity (PMID41267796), while crushed-seed Bond-Lader mood (PMID24412554) and mixed-product depression trials in hypothyroidism (p=.79) and multiple sclerosis were inconclusive, and a hemodialysis trial has unreported HADS results. Oil preparation, co-treatment, reporting discrepancy, and absence of toasted-seed or Parkinson trials keep the easing lean at minimal_signal. A distinct 2025 rat experiment reports lower forced-swim immobility under oral ethanol seed extract. Group estimates are graph-read and a separate general locomotor control is unavailable. It remains contextual for toasted seed and measured Parkinson depression.
